A person's certificate (ADR-0034, amendment 2026-10-15): --operator <person> makes a key and a request, a request as the argument with --sign <configuration> signs it. A node's: --node <node> with --cluster and --authority issues it a key and certificate from the cluster's authority (ADR-0015, amendment 2026-10-21); without --authority it makes the node's request to carry across an air gap, a carried request as the argument with --authority signs it, and a carried chain as the argument with --import <folder> imports it. The cluster's authority (ADR-0034, amendment 2026-10-22): --authority with --cluster and no node sets it up, --publish the address it publishes at; --inspect, --revoke, --export and --backup act on it. One act a line, and none of these options on another command but --out on database ().

member.name: T:Xmip.Cli.MeasureCommand
member.summary: xmip measure [scope]: the six figures at a scope, the cluster when none is named — Streams, Messages, Journeys, bytes, Retrying, Failed, in the order every surface says them (ADR-0027 clause 5). A figure the runtime has not published is a dash, never a zero. With --follow, one JSON Lines record each time the figures change.
member.remarks: Totals here, a rate in the prompt, and that is deliberate (ADR-0052, amendment 2026-09-20; ADR-0014's amendment asks that a change either reach every surface or name the one it did not). An invocation is one sample: it has no interval to divide by, and a rate taken from a single reading would be the average over the whole of the publisher's uptime — the very number the owner retired from the prompt. The prompt is a line that is always there and reads two publications; a command is a question asked once. With --follow there are samples, and the JSON Lines records already carry the figures and the scope for each one, so a program computes the rate exactly from two documents rather than being handed a rounded one (ADR-0014 clause 10: --json is for a program). The web board already says a rate in words beside each tile (English.Flow), so the executable is the one surface showing a total alone, and it says so here.

member.name: T:Xmip.Cli.MessageCommand
member.summary: xmip message: the Messages that failed, listed, and Retry or Dismiss on one (runtime-model.md section 13; ADR-0013). A Message travels to one Send Port on each Journey; when every Send Location of its Port failed its tries it is written Failed and waits in its Port's queue. With none named, every one that failed at or beneath --location is listed, Port by Port — how many wait, and a page of them with why, read from Xmip Storage in the process that runs the node or as its publication carries them; with one named, the act is the command, as the PowerShell module takes it as a parameter. How the list is read and the act reaches the node is the surface's; only the rendering is here. A list exits 0 when it is an answer, none failing among them, and 1 when it is not: the surface cannot list failed Messages, or asked and Xmip Storage did not answer. An act exits 0 when it was applied or left for the node, 1 when it was not, 2 for a line that names no node.
